title: Build and Diagnose a Safe Technical System
summary: Integrate a simulated server, operating system, network, monitoring signal, and technical record.
objectives: Use safe evidence to diagnose a controlled technical scenario.
Document the process and communicate a reasoned next step.

vocab.def: A process of gathering information to understand a problem.
The settings that determine how a system operates.
A considered explanation of what was learned and what could improve.

sections.heading: Project environment
sections.body: Use an approved browser simulation, disposable Linux sandbox, synthetic network map, or structured paper scenario. The system should include a server or service, a network path, a monitoring clue, and one controlled fault.

sections.heading: Project process
sections.body: Record the objective, environment, safety classification, observations, evidence, hypothesis, safe test, result, documentation, and escalation decision. Do not interact with production systems or real learner data.

sections.heading: Communicate the result
sections.body: Explain what you found, what remains uncertain, and what a qualified next step would be. Completing this lesson does not prove lab completion, project review, or professional competency.

practice.prompt: Before presenting, check that your project record separates observation from hypothesis and includes a safe boundary for the next action.

project.title: Build and Diagnose a Safe Technical System

options: Safe, evidence-based technical reasoning in a controlled environment

lab.objective: Complete a controlled technical scenario using only approved synthetic or disposable systems.

reflectionPrompt: Which technical system did you understand more clearly after the project, and what would you learn next?
